response.sql: WITH inv AS (SELECT invoice_number, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count, SUM(CASE WHEN derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL THEN derived_product_cost END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL THEN derived_total_cost END), 0) AS cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY invoice_number), avgr AS (SELECT AVG(cost_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM inv) SELECT inv.invoice_number, inv.cost_ratio, inv.line_item_count, inv.cost_ratio / NULLIF(avgr.avg_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio FROM inv CROSS JOIN avgr WHERE avgr.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL ORDER BY (inv.cost_ratio / NULLIF(avgr.avg_ratio, 0)) IS NULL, relative_ratio DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: An invoice's ratio is SUM(derived_product_cost)/SUM(derived_total_cost) over its line items, using only lines where both values are non-null. A zero total gives a NULL ratio.
The average ratio across all invoices is the simple average of the per-invoice ratios. Invoices with a NULL ratio are skipped, and each invoice has equal weight.
The line item count is the number of Invoice_Line_Items rows for the invoice, including rows with missing cost values.
If the average ratio is zero, the relative figure is NULL, which avoids division by zero. Those rows sort last.

alternatives.interpretation: Each invoice's ratio is the average of its per-line ratios (product cost / total cost for each line), instead of the ratio of sums. The line item count is unchanged.
